pass_b_english: Heavenly indeed, and most fittingly, he names the vocation that comes through Christ. For the God of all graciously bestows on those summoned through him not fleeting blessings nor the transient gifts given by the law through Moses to the ancients, but rather the very things that those once called have chosen—namely, eternal life—which he sustains and secures as an irrevocable possession.

We too have been designated heavenly in another way, with Christ taking the lead, and the way and the door having become ours. And truly Paul says, 'Just as we have borne the image of the earthly, let us also bear the image of the heavenly' (1 Corinthians 15:49), and again, 'The first man is from the earth, earthly; the second is from heaven' (1 Corinthians 15:47). Such as the earthly one is, such are the earthly people; and such as the heavenly one is, such are the heavenly people. Therefore we have become heavenly, for we are being shaped into Christ through the Spirit, who comes from heaven.

And because of this, even as we walk upon the earth, we hold our citizenship in heaven. We have not approached in equal measure the ancient manifestations of God—those accompanied by blazing fire, darkness, gloom, tempest, trumpet blast, and the voice of words—but we have drawn near rather to Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, amidst myriads of angels in festal assembly, the congregation of the firstborn whose names are inscribed in heaven, before the Judge who is God of all, and the spirits of the just made perfect.
